title: Digimind vs Zignal Labs vs Critical Mention: Budget-Conscious Crisis Monitoring Compared
summary: These three names still cluster together in every budget crisis monitoring search. Here's what each one actually is today, what it costs, and what's real.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Digimind, Zignal Labs, and Critical Mention still cluster together in nearly every "budget crisis monitoring tools" search — a grouping that's now more historical accident than current fact. Digimind no longer exists as a standalone product; it was folded into Onclusive Social in October 2024. Zignal Labs was acquired by Intercontinental Exchange in October 2025 and now sells exclusively to national-security and defense buyers, not brand or PR teams. Critical Mention is the only one of the three still selling directly to brand and PR teams as a standalone product, starting around $2,500-$10,000/year and pairing broadcast TV/radio coverage with digital and social alerts.


Type "budget crisis monitoring tools" into a search bar and these three names cluster together almost every time — same review sites, same comparison charts, same pricing tables. That clustering used to reflect a real, comparable set of options. It doesn't reflect much of anything today.


Two of the three companies behind these names have gone through changes significant enough that the old comparison no longer holds — one absorbed into a parent brand, one redirected to an entirely different buyer. Evaluate them as if they're still three parallel choices, and you'll waste a cycle chasing a demo that either doesn't exist under that name anymore or routes to a sales team that was never selling to you in the first place. Here's what each name actually means today, what it costs, and what's still real.


## Why do these three names keep showing up together?


They cluster together because search engines and review sites index by category, not by current company status — "budget PR/crisis monitoring tool" pulled in all three years ago, and that index has largely stuck even as two of the three companies changed what they sell.


Digimind, Zignal Labs, and Critical Mention were genuine peers around 2020-2022: mid-market monitoring tools competing on price against enterprise suites like Brandwatch and Meltwater. Since then, each has taken a different path — one rebranded entirely, one pivoted its buyer base, one stayed put. Review sites and comparison content rarely get updated fast enough to reflect that, so the same three names keep appearing side by side long after the comparison stopped being apples-to-apples.


## What does each of these three names actually refer to today?


**Digimind** no longer exists as a distinct product. Onclusive (Symphony Technology Group-backed) acquired Digimind in July 2022, ran it under light co-branding for two years, then fully renamed it "Onclusive Social" in October 2024.` digimind.com` now redirects entirely to` onclusive.com` (Source:[Onclusive — Social Listening Product Page, 2026](https://onclusive.com/products/social-listening/) ). For the full rebrand timeline and what Onclusive Social covers today, see our[Digimind alternatives breakdown](https://syncly.app/blog/best-digimind-alternatives-now-that-it-s-onclusive-social) .


**Zignal Labs** was acquired by Intercontinental Exchange, Inc. (NYSE: ICE — the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange) on October 29, 2025. Its current homepage positions the company exclusively as "Agentic Intelligence for National Security," organized around three pillars — People, Places, Position — for government, defense, and protective-intelligence buyers, with zero brand, PR, or crisis-comms framing anywhere on the site (Source:[Zignal Labs homepage, 2026](https://zignallabs.com/) ;[Signalbase — Zignal Labs Acquired by ICE, 2025](https://www.trysignalbase.com/news/acquisitions/zignal-labs-acquired-by-ice-acquisition) ). The pivot has deepened since, not reversed — Zignal launched "Zignal AI" at a Special Operations Forces industry conference in May 2026 (Source:[GlobeNewswire, 2026-05-18](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/05/18/3296553/0/en/zignal-labs-launches-zignal-ai-to-deliver-structured-intelligence-for-mission-systems-partners-and-agent-driven-workflows.html) ). More on what teams that used to rely on it have moved to: our[Zignal Labs alternatives roundup](https://syncly.app/blog/best-zignal-labs-alternatives-for-crisis-ready-teams-in-2026) .


**Critical Mention** is the one name in this trio that still means what it used to. It was acquired by Onclusive in mid-2022 too, but operates today as a distinct, standalone-branded subsidiary — "Critical Mention, an Onclusive Company" — still selling directly to brand and PR teams, still demo-gated but still purchasable (Source:[Critical Mention — About Us, 2026](https://www.criticalmention.com/about-us/) ). See our[Critical Mention alternatives roundup](https://syncly.app/blog/best-critical-mention-alternatives-for-broadcast-social-monitoring-in-2026) for how it stacks up against other broadcast-monitoring options specifically.


## How do Digimind, Zignal Labs, and Critical Mention pricing compare?


Only two of these three have a current price a brand or PR team could actually pay.


**Critical Mention** is the cheaper of the two real options by a wide margin — third-party analysis puts real contracts at roughly $2,500 to $10,000+ a year depending on modules, still quote-only (Source:[Prowly — Critical Mention Pricing and Alternatives, 2025](https://prowly.com/magazine/critical-mention-pricing/) ).


**Onclusive Social (formerly Digimind)** sits noticeably higher — around €15,000/year starting, usage-based on query and mention volume, no self-serve checkout though a free trial is available (Source:[Onclusive — Social Listening Product Page, 2026](https://onclusive.com/products/social-listening/) ).


**Zignal Labs'** old pricing — historically $25,000/year entry, $50,000-$150,000+/year enterprise range — is only useful as historical context for why teams once bracketed it with the other two. It isn't a figure a brand team could act on today (Source:[ITQlick — Zignal Labs Pricing, 2026](https://www.itqlick.com/zignal-labs/pricing) ).

## Which of the three, if any, still fits a budget-conscious brand or PR team?


If you need broadcast exposure covered — TV or radio coverage that could break before anything shows up online — **Critical Mention** is both the only real option here and the cheapest, with 2,500+ stations across every US Nielsen DMA plus Europe and the Middle East (Source:[Critical Mention — Broadcast Monitoring, 2026](https://www.criticalmention.com/media-monitoring/broadcast-monitoring/) ).


If your primary signal is a sentiment spike on digital and[social listening](https://syncly.app/social/solution/social-listening) channels rather than a broadcast segment, **Onclusive Social's** named Sentinel feature — real-time alerts on negative-sentiment, keyword, or hashtag spikes — is built specifically for that, at a meaningfully higher price floor (Source:[Onclusive — Social Listening Product Page, 2026](https://onclusive.com/products/social-listening/) ).


**Zignal Labs** doesn't belong in this decision at all anymore — there's no version of a brand-team crisis workflow that leads back to its current national-security product.


Neither of the two remaining options catches what happens when a crisis starts as a spoken TikTok video or an[on-screen product callout](https://syncly.app/social/feature/video-analysis) without a caption mentioning the brand — a growing blind spot as 97% of TikTok videos mentioning brands don't tag the official account (Source:[Octolens — TikTok Monitoring, 2026](https://octolens.com/tiktok-monitoring) ).[Syncly Social](https://syncly.app/social) is built around Audio Intelligence (transcribing what's said) and AI Vision (reading what's shown) together, catching[untagged mentions](https://syncly.app/social/feature/untagged-mentions) across TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts — not a replacement for broadcast monitoring or a competitor-analysis suite, but the piece neither surviving option was built to catch.


## Key Takeaways


-


Digimind, Zignal Labs, and Critical Mention still appear together in "budget crisis monitoring" searches, but only one of the three still sells to that buyer today.


-


Digimind was fully absorbed into Onclusive Social in October 2024 — it no longer exists as a separate product, though the underlying tool is still active.


-


Zignal Labs was acquired by Intercontinental Exchange in October 2025 and now sells exclusively to national-security and defense buyers — it doesn't belong in a brand or PR team's shortlist anymore.


-


Critical Mention is the only one of the three still standalone and still selling to brand/PR teams, and it's also the cheapest, at roughly $2,500-$10,000+/year.


-


Onclusive Social costs more (~€15,000/year) but has a named real-time crisis-alerting feature, Sentinel, for teams whose primary risk is digital/social sentiment rather than broadcast.


The next time a "budget crisis monitoring" list groups these three together, treat it as a leftover of an old category, not a current menu. Two of the names have moved on; only one is still answering the phone.
